content: R3F auto-disposes geometries/materials on unmount by default; explicit manual dispose() is mainly needed for (a) objects created outside R3F's declarative tree (e.g. imperatively in useEffect/useMemo) which must be cleaned up in a useEffect cleanup function, (b) dynamically swapped geometries -- every state change that creates a fresh BufferGeometry leaks VRAM unless the old one is disposed, so recomputing a toolpath's geometry every playback frame instead of updating an existing buffer will exhaust memory within minutes, (c) GLTF/loaded model textures, which should be traversed and disposed manually since useLoader's cache keeps them alive. dispose={null} on an R3F primitive opts out of auto-disposal for reused/shared assets.
